report:
### Conclusion
The claim that drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19 is **false**. There is no scientific evidence supporting garlic water as a cure or preventive treatment for COVID-19, and the claim has been repeatedly debunked by public health authorities and fact-checkers.

### Evidence Overview
* **Lack of Evidence for a Cure:** Health experts and organizations, including the World Health Organization (WHO), have confirmed that there is no evidence that consuming garlic or drinking boiled garlic water cures COVID-19 (https://factcheck.afp.com/health-experts-refute-false-claims-drinking-boiled-garlic-water-cures-novel-coronavirus, https://www.factcheck.org/2020/02/fake-coronavirus-cures-part-2-garlic-isnt-a-cure/).
* **Antimicrobial vs. Antiviral Properties:** While garlic is a healthy food that possesses some general antimicrobial properties, WHO notes that no evidence shows eating garlic has protected people from SARS-CoV-2 (https://www.itv.com/news/2020-03-10/garlic-spraying-yourself-with-chlorine-and-hot-baths-do-not-prevent-coronavirus-world-health-organisation-warns). 
* **Potential Risks of Excessive Use:** According to Sylvie Briand, WHO director of global infectious hazard preparedness, while garlic provides general nutritional benefits, overconsuming garlic in attempt to treat illness can actually cause health issues or be detrimental to a person (https://www.boomlive.in/world/fake-news-covid-19-cure-onion-ginger-garlic-lemon-tonic-11939).
